newsitem.title: UK: Britain summons French envoy over truckers row.
newsitem.headline: Britain summons French envoy over truckers row.

text.p: Britain's Transport Secretary has summoned the French ambassador to express the government's concern over the stranding of British lorries by the French truckers' highway blockade, officials said on Friday.

Sir George Young told Ambassador Jean Guieguinou that he was particularly worried about reports that French police had failed to intervene when British drivers were apparently threatened with violence.

"He was looking to be updated on the current position and emphasise his concern about British drivers caught in the queues and reinforce the view that prompt compensations should be given," a transport department spokesman said.
"But it would be too strong to call it a dressing down," he said of Thursday's meeting.
Sir George had no plans to fly to Paris for talks with the French government, he added.

French union leaders said on Friday they were keen to negotiate an end to the 12-day strike that is strangling the French economy. But they want the government to guarantee by decree payment for all hours worked.
The strike, in the crucial pre-Christmas commercial period, has cost European food and haulage industries tens of millions of dollars a day, prompting protests from France's neighbours.
